artifacts.note: intermediate Lua/Julia summaries live under results/m4; raw candidate JSONL and diagnostic traces live under results/raw (gitignored)

caveats: Same-core speedup compares Lua repeat-timed throughput against one post-warmup Julia pass; it is indicative, not benchmark-grade.
Julia t1 headline is the t1 parallel pass (one worker); the serial pass is reported alongside it. Thread scaling compares parallel passes at t1 versus tN.

Thread counts above nproc are capped before launch; options.threads_requested vs options.threads_capped records the difference, and each Julia entry records the summary's requested vs actual thread count.
Allocation is process-wide and measured on the serial path only; --alloc adds an extra untimed serial pass so per-candidate bytes exclude JIT/library warmup.
Peak memory is whole-process RSS (runtime and JIT included) from scripts/bench_process.py; for threads > 1 it is not a per-worker figure.
Julia per-candidate latency is derived by summing the reset/sim/extract phase stats; the summary carries mean/p50/p99 per phase but no per-phase max, so max_ms is null.
Lua per-candidate latency uses phases.total (us) and averages the per-repeat summary quantiles across repeats, not a pooled quantile.
Full-grid reference numbers are stride 1 from session 1; this benchmark is stride 20. Do not compare per-candidate rates across strides.
Tracing-on timing is diagnostic only; it is reported in the diagnostic block and never merged into the main workload table.
The Lua harness is single-threaded; thread counts apply to Julia only. All runs are same-host.
The M4 correctness gate is the session-1 full-grid parity sweep; the stride-20 comparator block is informational.

diagnostic.method: one untraced and one traced single serial Julia pass (threads=1, no --verify-serial, no --alloc), same stride/level/balls; timing-on is diagnostic only and is never merged into the main workload table
diagnostic.outcome_equality_check: sha256 of the canonical JSONL result rows; equality means tracing did not change any candidate field
diagnostic.preferred_workload_note: circles_small is the preferred diagnostic workload: fast enough to keep the trace I/O measurable without dominating the run

traced.peak_memory_method_note: resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss after waiting for the single measured child; the kernel high-water mark (VmHWM), same quantity as GNU time -v
traced.trace_bytes_per_step_note: sum of per-candidate trace file sizes / total simulated steps; each file includes a one-line header, so the marginal per-step cost is slightly below this value

untraced.peak_memory_method_note: resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss after waiting for the single measured child; the kernel high-water mark (VmHWM), same quantity as GNU time -v

full_grid_reference.note: Full-grid throughput is stride 1 from session 1; the timed benchmark in this report is stride 20 (91 candidates per workload). Per-candidate rates and tails are not directly comparable between stride 1 and stride 20.
